subject: Fix prism.py's comment-family taxonomy -- comment/code separation was completely broken for all 58 languages (#386) (#389)

Fix prism.py's comment-family taxonomy -- comment/code separation was completely broken for all 58 languages (#386) (#389)

Root cause (see #386 for the full empirical investigation): split_streams()
special-cased exactly three family names ("recursive_c_style",
"column_sensitive", "single_line_only") for dedicated stripping logic, and
fell back to a REGEX_MATRIX built from comment_definitions.get(
"mechanical_families", {}) for everything else -- a key nothing ever wrote
(#378's original dead-key finding). But even fixing that key name alone
wouldn't have been enough: none of the three special-cased names, nor the
matrix-building fam_keys ("c_style_comment", "single_line_only",
"embedded_syntax", "multi_style_dash"), matched the REAL per-language
"lexical_family" taxonomy actually used across language_standards.py
(standard_block: 29 languages, line_exclusive: 21, recursive_block: 3,
positional_anchored: 3, block_exclusive: 1, non_lexical: 1). So every
single language fell through to the always-empty generic stripper --
verified empirically: `Prism(...).split_streams("x = 1  # comment",
"python")` returned the comment still embedded in code_stream, comment_
stream empty, even for Python.

This went undetected because test_prism.py's entire suite ran against a
hand-built mock config (MOCK_COMMENT_DEFS/MOCK_LANG_DEFS) using a
fictional, internally-consistent taxonomy that matched split_streams()'s
special cases but never matched the real config -- every test passed
without ever exercising real data.

Fix: renamed prism.py's three special-cased family checks and
_compile_regex_matrix()'s fam_key checks to the real taxonomy
(recursive_c_style -> recursive_block, column_sensitive ->
positional_anchored, single_line_only -> line_exclusive, c_style_comment ->
standard_block), plus the default "lexical_family" fallback. Verified
empirically post-fix: C, Python, Rust, and COBOL (one language per
previously-broken family) now correctly separate comments from code.
Contained entirely to prism.py -- no changes to gitgalaxy_config.py or any
of the 58 language definitions, per the scoped plan in #386.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS, tracked but not fixed here (per the approved scope --
see #386):
- "standard_block"'s real delimiter list has 9 entries (C-style, SQL/
  Lua-style --/--[[/]], Haskell-style {-/-}, and a trailing #), but the
  regex-building branch only uses the first 3 (// and /* */). The ~24
  C-style languages in this family (c, cpp, java, javascript, go, etc.)
  are fully fixed; the 5 that don't use C-style delimiters at all
  (sqlite, lua, haskell, powershell, perl) are unchanged from before --
  not a regression, since nothing was stripped for them either way.
- "block_exclusive" (xml, 1 language) has its own separately malformed
  delimiter data (["", "--!>"]) and isn't covered by this fix.
- golden_master.json is not regenerated here. This fix will very likely
  shift LOC/signal counts across most of the corpus now that comments
  actually stop leaking

pr_body_start: Closes #1222 **Problem:** The tokenizer in `Prism` was incorrectly matching quotes inside comments (e.g., apostrophes in `// doesn't`) as the start of string literals. This caused it to mask all the code following the comment until the next valid quote, effectively merging those lines. The subsequent pass to strip comments would then indiscriminately delete all that masked code, leading to severe function extraction failures (as seen in `site/tools/search.js` where 9 out of 10 methods were swallowed). **Solution:** Refactored `_strip_segment_comments` in `gitgalaxy/core/prism.py` to process literals and comments in a single atomic regex pass. By evaluating both concurrently in a single alternation, the engine correctly gives precedence to whichever sequence starts first. If a comment begins, any quotes within it are safely ignored. **Testing:** - Added `test_prism_issue_1222.py` as a permanent regression test to ensure quotes in comments never again disrupt function extraction. - Ran full `pytest` suite, resulting in `6815` passing tests. - Regenerated the full-precision and zero-dependency golden masters to safely bless the intentionally improved downstream structural metrics and function extraction recall.

commit_message:
fix(regex): resolve ReDoS timeout in typescript args extraction (#2156)

Co-authored-by: Joe Esquibel <squid-protocol@users.noreply.github.com>
pr_title: fix(regex): resolve ReDoS timeout in typescript args extraction
pr_body_start:
### What
This PR fixes a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in the `args` extraction rule for TypeScript, which was causing the CI pipeline to timeout after 180 seconds.

### Why
The `args` regex had an overlapping alternative in its nested parentheses matcher: `\((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\)|\((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*\))*\)`. The middle alternative `\([^()]*\)` was fully subsumed by the third alternative, which matched up to depth 2. This created a classic ReDoS structure `(A|B|C)*` where B and C overlap, causing catastrophic backtracking on long inputs that ultimately fail to match.

### How
Removed the redundant `\([^()]*\)` alternative from the three branches of the TypeScript `args` regex, converting it to `\((?:[^()]|\((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*\))*\)`. This maintains the exact same depth-3 matching capabilities while eliminating the exponential backtracking. Verified by running the TypeScript test suite.

* fix(core-engine): the orphan census counts references, not name repetitions (#2727, #2728)

`orphaned_logic` was decided by `token_counts[name] <= 1` over the whole code
stream, so whether a function read as orphaned depended on how many times the
language's syntax writes its name -- not on whether anything calls it. Three
distinct defects came out of that one line.

1. #2727 -- syntax that repeats the name masked every orphan. Ada closes with

   type signature above the equation: the count is already 2 before anything
   calls the function. livecode reported 3 orphans across the crucible where
   the scoped test finds 127; ada and livecode reported 0 per file in
   keyword-rosetta against a 2.50 baseline.

   The test is now scoped to each function's own span, with a correction the
   issue's fix shape missed. The span does NOT reliably contain the
   declaration: shell's Mode-B spans start at the `{`, so a K&R `make_module()`
   on the previous line sits outside its own body, and ruby's spans are offset
   outright (66 of 132 sampled functions). Counting outside the span naively
   makes the declaration itself read as a reference: ruby fell 51 -> 44
   orphans that way, html 5 -> 2, shell 8 -> 3, losing real ones. So when the
   span holds no occurrence of the name, the definition site is outside it by
   construction and exactly one outside occurrence is discounted. With the
   correction no language decreases for this reason.

   containing `-`, `:` or `.`, so any name holding one counted ZERO and

commit_message:
fix(#2978): run the security lens on inert data formats (#3009)

galaxyscope.py classified plaintext/markdown/json/yaml/csv as "inert" and
skipped Phase 5.5 (SecurityLens.scan_content) for all of them, so a
hardcoded credential in an ordinary config.yaml/settings.json was
invisible to sec_hardcoded_secrets -- the filename/extension-based
CRITICAL-LEAK shunt in aperture.py only catches credential-named files
(.env, .pem), not an arbitrary config with a secret embedded in it.

The lens now runs on all five inert formats by default, opt-out via a new
SECURITY_SCAN_INERT_FORMATS config flag (wired through config_resolver.py
the same way STRICT_IMPORT_MODE/FIREWALL_NETWORK_WEIGHTING are) for repos
where that trades too much doc/config noise (README code-fence examples,
CI YAML secrets: blocks) for the extra coverage.

signal_processor.py's Static Literature Override separately blanket-zeroed
the whole risk vector for markdown/plaintext/rst/text (by design, for
dimensions like cognitive load and authorship centralization that
genuinely don't apply to prose) -- carved out secrets_risk there too,
reusing the same graduated _calc_secrets_risk formula non-doc languages
get, so a real leak in a README doesn't silently score 0 regardless of the
raw hit count.

Also fixes tests/tools/update_golden_master.py, which was missing the
GITGALAXY_DISABLE_GIT_HISTORY=1 env var test_golden_crucible.py already
sets (added for #2976) -- without it, a bless run against a full local
corpus clone picks up real git-log-derived signals (Architect/Authorship
Centralization/Raw Churn Frequency) the check path never sees, producing
~8500 unrelated differences on every future bless. This is gitgalaxy#3005's
root cause.

perf: kill ReDoS + O(N^2) splice hot paths behind v2.7.0 speed outliers (#3043)

Ranking the v2.7.0 batch (gitgalaxy-raw-output speed_summary.json) by
actual/predicted against the published rate model surfaced a handful of
large-repo outliers. Drilling in found three distinct root causes, all
fixed here with byte-for-byte match parity (pure speed, no detection change):

1. zig::class_start — catastrophic backtracking. A bounded `{0,150}` gap fed a
   `*`-group nesting `+` over overlapping whitespace/word classes; on ordinary
   `const x = ...` lines with no type keyword the engine exploded (ghostty's
   DiskCache.zig: one 18KB file took 406s). Rewrote only the step-over as a
   bounded {0,8} of non-overlapping single-line branches; the tempered gap is
   unchanged. 406s -> 0.5ms; 0 mismatches / 4,971 corpus files.

2. detector.py::_is_orphan — O(functions x filesize). The #2727 rewrite replaced
   a whole-file frequency table with a per-function finditer over the entire
   code_stream. Precompute one word-token offset index and answer each function
   by bisect; non-\w names keep the exact fallback. 0 mismatches / 2,275 fns.

3. detector.py line numbering — O(matches x filesize) via per-match/per-class
   `code_stream.count("\n", 0, idx)`. Precompute newline offsets once per
   stream/segment, look up by bisect (algebraically identical).

4. yaml::func_start + class_start — ReDoS that only fires on the indentation-safe
   stream (blank lines make the bounded step-over backtrack). Same linear
   rewrite; 40s -> 2ms; 0 mismatches / ~394 files.

Combined splice on sokol_gfx.h (1MB, 928 fns): 16.1s -> 1.7s. End-to-end
(licensed, no friction delay): ghostty 477s->15.6s, ansible 156s->18.7s,
esphome 110s->26.5s -- all now on the rate-model fit line.

Full extraction + core_engine suite: 8450 passed, 0 failures. Ruff clean.

commit_message:
perf(detector): skip =-less lines before the var-decl backtracking regex (#3063)

From exploring the nx (TypeScript) speed residual: _var_decl_pattern
(^[ \t]*(?:[^=\n]{0,80}[ \t]+)?([A-Za-z_]\w{0,63})[ \t]*=(?!=)) backtracked its
greedy [^=\n]{0,80} prefix across every line before failing -- and it can never
match a line without a bare '=' (the pattern requires one and [^=\n] can't cross
a newline). Profiling put this at ~a quarter of splice() on large TS files.

Fix: iterate lines and skip those without '='; .match per line is identical to
the original re.M ^-anchored finditer (anchors at line start, <=1 match per line,
in line order), so every equations count is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Parity: identifier lists identical over 800 real TS/JS files (0 mismatches); BOTH
golden-crucible legs pass (full-precision + zero-dependency, corpus-wide
extraction unchanged); 8,124 extraction tests, ruff, mypy all green.

Impact: 8.2x on the var-decl pass, ~15% on a 561KB TS file. NOTE: this reduces
per-file CPU work, but a whole-repo scan's PASS_1 is parallel across cores, so
nx's wall-time is parallelism-bound and barely moves (77.1s -> 76.4s) -- nx's 4x
residual is structural (heavy TS per-LOC work), not a single hot loop. Shipped as
a CPU/backtracking-efficiency fix that helps the whole corpus and any
single-threaded path.

A hit seen in two pieces counts once. ## Class / Sibling gaps Class: every `THREAT_SIGNATURES` key on a line of 250+ characters (13 keys).
